sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house in Maryville, TN?
sections.html:
Maryville sellers can hire an agent, handle the sale alone, or take cash for the house exactly as it is. Repair costs, timing and your patience for showings decide which is better.

Maryville is growing slowly. The Census Bureau shows 32,442 residents in July 2025, only 1.7% above the 2020 base. Owners live in 67.5% of homes, those homes have a 2020-2024 median value of $358,100, and 90.3% of residents were in the same house a year before the survey.

  • An agent fits a well-kept house and an owner who can wait for the right buyer.
  • A solo sale works if you are comfortable with the contract and closing papers.
  • Cash is the practical choice when repairs, a tenant or an estate complicate a traditional sale.

Maryville is the seat of Blount County, set in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains, and its twin city Alcoa lies to the north. Wikipedia records that John Craig built Fort Craig here in 1785 and that the settlement became a city in 1795 and took the name of Mary Grainger Blount, wife of the territorial governor. Maryville College sits in town, and Chilhowee Mountain rises to the south.

The main routes are Broadway (U.S. 411 and 129), Lamar Alexander Parkway (U.S. 321, toward Townsend and the national park) and the Maryville-Alcoa Bypass toward Knoxville. Interstate 140 connects the area to McGhee Tyson Airport and West Knoxville. The Census Bureau's mean commute for workers is 23.3 minutes. Parks include the Bicentennial Greenbelt Park, the Maryville Alcoa Greenway and Sandy Springs Park.

Maryville has about 17 square miles of land at roughly 981 feet in elevation, with 12,207 households and a median gross rent of $1,157 for 2020-2024. July highs average 87 degrees and January lows average 29, so winters are mild compared with the higher Smokies country to the east.

sections.h2: What jobs and schools support Maryville home values?
sections.html:
The city's 2025 audit report names Denso Manufacturing Tennessee as the largest employer, with about 5,000 full-time employees since 1988, and Blount Memorial Hospital as the county's third largest at more than 2,700. Smith and Wesson headquarters, two Amazon locations and a BJ's Wholesale Club have added jobs more recently.

Maryville City Schools serves 5,619 students in eight schools, according to the same report, and the city put $9,422,500 from its general fund into school operations in fiscal 2025. The Census Bureau reports 93.7% of adults hold a high school diploma and 38.5% have a bachelor's degree or more, with a poverty rate of 6.7% and median household income of $81,963.

sections.h2: How do Maryville city and Blount County taxes work?
sections.html:
A Maryville house carries a city bill and a Blount County bill. The county rate fell to $1.29 on each $100 of assessed value for 2026, down from $1.59 in the three prior years, per the Blount County Trustee. The city's fiscal 2027 budget ordinance, on second reading in June 2026, funds the general fund with a $1.36 rate on each $100.

The Trustee's example makes the math concrete: a $250,000 house is assessed at $62,500, which yields a county bill of $806 at the $1.29 rate. The tax roll names whoever owned the house on January 1, and the Trustee says taxes are normally prorated at closing with the buyer becoming the responsible party. The county's calendar of important dates sets February 28 for the final day to pay the prior year's taxes and to apply for tax relief, and March 15 for greenbelt applications. Reach the Trustee at 865-273-5900 or the City of Maryville financial services office at 865-273-3456 for payoff figures.

sections.h2: What building codes and permits matter when selling in Maryville?
sections.html:
Maryville Codes Enforcement, at 416 West Broadway, administers building and property maintenance rules and takes calls at 865-273-3500. According to the city's codes page, the council adopted the 2024 International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Energy Conservation, Plumbing and Fire codes plus a 2024 Property Maintenance Code, all effective January 1, 2026. The 2017 National Electrical Code stays in force.

Ask the codes office which code edition applied to any work you permitted recently, since a buyer's contractor may ask. The city also adopted tougher penalties for construction and property maintenance violations under state law. If you remodeled without a permit, talk to the codes office before listing.

sections.h2: How does Maryville handle short-term rentals?
sections.html:
The city issues short-term rental unit permits and asks for a plan and a safety affidavit with each application. The planning office lists short-term rentals among its zoning topics, so confirm with it that your address is in a district where the use is allowed.

  • The application includes a sketch of the lot and floor plan showing bedrooms, beds, off-street parking and life safety equipment.
  • The owner swears an affidavit of life safety compliance covering UL 217 smoke alarms in and near each sleeping room and on each story, a carbon monoxide detector within 15 feet of bedrooms and a working fire extinguisher.
  • The equipment is subject to inspection before the permit is issued and afterward on reasonable notice.

If you are selling a short-term rental, tell the buyer which permit applies and call the city at 865-273-3500 to ask whether it transfers.

sections.h2: How does recording a deed work in Blount County?
sections.html:
Maryville deeds are filed with the Blount County Register of Deeds at 349 Court Street, phone 865-273-5880. The county's fee page lists $12 to record one or two pages, $5 for each added page and a $1 clerk fee, plus the state's deed transfer tax of 37 cents per $100.

The office requires the district, map and parcel numbers on every deed, along with the responsible taxpayer's name and address. Trust deeds and mortgages must carry the statement of maximum principal indebtedness for recording tax purposes. Originals are returned after recording if you include a stamped return envelope.

One local quirk is worth knowing. Maryville has more than 250 old platted alleys, and the city is closing the ones no longer needed. When an alley closes it usually reverts 50/50 to the owners on each side, and the city prepares quitclaim deeds for them at no cost and records them. If your lot touches a platted alley, ask planning whether it has been abandoned.

faqs.q: Is a Maryville house taxed by both the city and the county?
faqs.a: Yes. A house inside the city is billed by the City of Maryville and by Blount County, and each has its own rate. Ask both offices for a payoff before closing.

faqs.q: When are Blount County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Notices are mailed in early to mid-September and payable through the end of February. Taxes become delinquent on March 1, and 1.5% interest is added each month until paid.

faqs.q: Does Blount County reward early tax payment?
faqs.a: Yes. The county gives 2% off for payment through October and 1% for November, and the discount is already shown on the notice.

faqs.q: What will the Blount County Register of Deeds charge?
faqs.a: Recording runs $12 for a one- or two-page deed, $5 for each page after that and a $1 clerk fee, and the state transfer tax adds 37 cents on every $100 of the price. Confirm the total for your document with the office.

faqs.q: Which Maryville office handles codes and permits?
faqs.a: Call Maryville Codes Enforcement at 865-273-3500, at the Municipal Center, 416 West Broadway. The planning office answers at the same number.
